chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man said to him, 'May I be your ransom! A man who has recognized this matter (al-Wilayah) has confined himself to his house and does not introduce himself to anyone among his brethren.' He (the narrator) said: He (the Imam) then replied, 'How will this one gain deep understanding in his religion?'

key_terms.إِخْوَانِهِ: His brethren — fellow Shi'i Muslims who share the same religious conviction
key_terms.هَذَا الْأَمْرَ: This matter — a coded reference to al-Wilayah, the belief in the divinely-appointed authority of the Imams
key_terms.يَتَفَقَّهُ: To gain deep religious understanding (fiqh), implying thorough comprehension beyond surface knowledge

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about isolating yourself from Muslim community?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) responds to a question about a believer who, upon recognizing the truth of the Imamate (al-Wilayah), withdrew from society entirely and isolated himself at home. The Imam's rhetorical question — 'How will this person understand his religion?' — emphasizes that religious learning and deep understanding (tafaqquh) cannot be achieved in isolation; community engagement with fellow believers is essential to religious growth. This teaching is situated within a chapter dedicated to the necessity of seeking knowledge, underscoring that such necessity includes active participation in religious circles.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from the one who reported it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A man said to himasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! A man recognises this matter (Al-Wilayah), necessitates the (staying in) his house and does not introduce (himself) to anyone from his brethren’. So heasws said: ‘How can this one (be able to enhance) understanding in his Religion (without interacting with people)?’
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from one who narrated to him from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) the following. “A man said asked, ‘May Allah take my soul in your service, a man believes in this fact, (Leadership of Ahlul Bayt with Divine Authority) but keeps himself at home and does not acquaint himself with his brethren.”
Abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) said, “How he achieves good understanding of his religion?”
